lede: Tuesday's Town Council meeting is the one to watch this week — a newly seated Council takes up second reading of the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code, which would amend the Land Use Code on landscaping, trees, and historic review to meet state wildfire standards, and that vote matters for anyone who owns or rents in town. Also on Tuesday, the Housing Authority tackles a new primary-residency policy for dependents of multiple custodial households, and Thursday's Planning and Zoning Commission digs into three Town-owned development projects in the Accommodations 2 zone, including the Carhenge Redevelopment at 700 W Pacific.

notable.stake: Council votes second reading on wildfire code changes to Land Use Code.
Housing Authority sets new primary-residency policy affecting multi-custodial households.
P&Z reviews Town-owned Carhenge and two other major development projects.
